transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... honestly, I just can't seem to stay in my chair when I'm supposed to. It's getting embarrassing. Like, I'll be in the middle of a client interview—I'm a private investigator, by the way, mostly infidelity cases lately, which are just so depressing. You wouldn't believe the lengths people go to hide things. Just last week, I had a guy who rented a whole separate apartment under his dog's name! Who does that? Buster the Golden Retriever signing a lease, right? Anyway, where was I? Oh, right. During these interviews, or when I'm doing some tutoring on the side, or even at my book club—we're reading this historical fiction thing right now, lots of boats, not my favorite—I just keep getting up. I can't just sit and listen. People are definitely starting to notice, and it's becoming a problem.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Act on impulse? Hmm... no, not really. I mean, I don't think so. In my line of work, you really have to think things through, you know? Like on a stakeout, you can't just do whatever pops into your head. You have to plan ahead. Especially the snacks. You can't bring anything crunchy, like chips, because the sound echoes in a quiet car, and you definitely can't bring chocolate in July. I learned that the hard way last year. It was a hundred and two degrees out, and I had this whole bag of peanut butter cups... completely melted all over my favorite seat covers. They were these amazing vintage floral ones I found at this Sunday flea market. Oh, I love a good flea market. Have you ever been to the one out on Route 9? There's this one vendor who sells nothing but old brass doorknobs. Just boxes and boxes of them. I always wonder who is buying that many doorknobs, you know? Like, are they building a mansion? Anyway... wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my car?
Do you often find it hard to focus on what's being said or to follow through on instructions?

Focus on what's being said? No, not really. I'm actually a very good listener. You kind of have to be in my line of work, right? When you're interviewing a witness or a client, you have to catch every little detail they give you. Like last month, I was talking to this woman about her husband's erratic schedule, and she had the most fascinating accent. I think it was Scottish? Or maybe Irish. I always get those two mixed up. I actually went to Ireland right after I finished my bachelor's degree. Just backpacked around for three weeks with my best friend. It is incredibly green there, just like everyone says, but it rained almost every single day. I had to buy this massive, chunky wool sweater in Galway just to survive the dampness. It was so incredibly itchy! I actually still have it in my closet somewhere. I keep meaning to donate it, but I have this habit of holding onto things. Like, I still have my old college textbooks in a box in the garage. Why do I need a sociology textbook from 1996? I don't even like sociology. I really wanted to major in history, but my parents thought... wait, I'm sorry. What did you ask me? Something about instructions? Yeah, no, I don't have a problem following instructions. I'm fine with that.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting with your hands or feet when you're sitting still?

Fidgeting? Oh, yeah, all the time. Especially when I'm stuck at the computer combing through records. My foot is just constantly bouncing under the desk, and I'm usually clicking a pen. Click, click, click. I actually had a client get really annoyed by the clicking once. He was this very high-strung guy, a dentist, I think. Or maybe an orthodontist? He was obsessed with teeth, anyway. Kept staring at my mouth while we were talking, which is so distracting. I use this whitening toothpaste, but I drink so much coffee I feel like it just cancels it out completely. I just got this new espresso machine for my kitchen, and it's this gorgeous cherry red color. It matches my stand mixer perfectly. I love baking, though I never have the time anymore. I make a really good banana bread. The secret is adding a little bit of sour cream to the batter. Keeps it moist. But anyway, yeah, when I'm at the desk, I'm shifting around so much that I literally lose my place in what I'm reading. I'll have to start the whole page over because I just can't sit still. Wait, what were we just talking about? Did you ask about my desk setup?
Did you have trouble sitting still when you were a kid?

As a kid? Oh, absolutely. My mother still jokes about it. She always says I treated every single classroom like a crime scene I had to pace through. Which is funny, considering what I do for a living now, right? But yeah, my grade-school report cards always said the exact same thing—that I was bright, but I just couldn't stay in my seat or wait my turn. 

Waiting my turn was the absolute worst. Especially during recess. We had this huge metal slide at my elementary school. You know the kind that gets burning hot in the afternoon sun? They don't make them like that anymore. Now everything is plastic and covered in that soft rubber mulch stuff. Which is probably safer, obviously. I actually read this article the other day about playground safety regulations and how they've changed since the 80s. It was in this waiting room... I think I was getting my oil changed? No, wait, it was the dentist. The one I told you about! The guy obsessed with teeth. His waiting room had the most outdated magazines. I mean, who wants to read a three-year-old copy of Field & Stream? I don't even fish. I tried fishing once with my uncle down in Florida, but the boat was rocking so much I got completely seasick. Worst weekend of my life. The humidity down there is just unbearable, too, it ruins my hair the second I step off the plane. 

Anyway... wait, what did you ask me? Did you ask about my mom?
Are these difficulties with sitting still and focusing causing problems for you at work or in your personal relationships?

Problems at work? Yeah, actually, it is. It's really starting to cost me professionally. I've missed details in a couple of investigations lately because I just can't stay still long enough to read through the files properly. And I've definitely irritated some clients. Like that dentist! And it's not just clients, either. The junior detectives at the agency are getting less and less willing to debrief with me. They say they feel steamrolled because I just talk over them and can't sit through their reports. 

Which is frustrating, because I really like mentoring the younger investigators. We have this one new girl, she's fresh out of college, maybe 22? She wears these incredible vintage suits to the office. I asked her where she shops, and she said she thrifts everything. I can never find anything good at thrift stores. It's always just racks of 90s windbreakers and clothes that smell like mothballs. My grandmother's house always smelled like mothballs. She had this beautiful cedar chest at the foot of her bed where she kept all her good linens. I inherited it when she passed away, but it's just sitting in my guest room right now because it doesn't really match my decor. I have a very modern, minimalist thing going on in my house, lots of glass and chrome. It's a nightmare to keep clean, honestly. You see every single fingerprint on the glass coffee table. I must wipe that thing down three times a day. I use this citrus cleaner that smells amazing, like real grapefruits. I love grapefruits, but you can't eat them if you take certain medications, right? I read that somewhere. 

Anyway... wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my house?
Do you think your main problem is that you can't pay attention or that you just can't stay still?

I think it's definitely the staying still part. That's actually what brings me in, honestly. I just keep getting up when I'm supposed to stay put. Like during client interviews, I'll just stand up and start walking around the room. Or when I do these little tutoring sessions on the side, or even at my book club! People are really starting to notice that I just cannot sit and listen. 

Which is embarrassing at book club, especially. We're reading this new thriller right now, and it is so incredibly predictable. I figured out who the killer was by chapter three. I mean, being a private investigator kind of ruins mystery novels for you, you know? But the hostess, Brenda, she always makes these amazing charcuterie boards. She gets these little imported cheeses from this specialty shop downtown. I went there once to try and buy some, but parking downtown is an absolute nightmare. They have those new digital meters where you have to type in your license plate, and I always forget my license plate number. I had to take a picture of it on my phone so I wouldn't have to walk back to my car. 

My phone is completely out of storage space right now, though, because I take too many pictures of my cat. He's a Maine Coon, huge, like twenty pounds. He sheds everywhere. I had to buy a special vacuum just for the pet hair. It's one of those cordless ones, but the battery life on it is terrible. I can barely get through the living room before it completely dies on me. 

Anyway... wait, what did you ask me? Did you ask if I read a lot?
Do you often feel anxious or restless when you're unable to get up and move around?

Anxious? Um, I don't know if I'd call it anxious, really. I just... I don't really know if I feel restless either, honestly. I've never really thought about it like that. I just know I get up. It's not like a nervous thing, I don't think? 

Speaking of nervous, though, my cat—the Maine Coon I was just telling you about—he gets so incredibly nervous whenever the mail carrier comes to the door. It's the strangest thing. The mail carrier is this really nice guy, too, he always wears those little blue shorts even when it's freezing outside. I don't know how postal workers do it. I could never wear shorts in the winter. My circulation is terrible. My hands are always freezing. I bought these expensive thermal gloves for stakeouts, the kind with the little touch-screen fingertips so you can still use your phone? But they never actually work on the screen. You always end up having to take the glove off anyway, which completely defeats the purpose. 

I was on a stakeout last week, actually, sitting in my car for four hours straight. Well, not straight, obviously, because I kept having to get out and stretch my legs. I parked near this amazing little bakery, and the smell of the sourdough bread was just driving me crazy. Sourdough is my absolute favorite. I tried making a sourdough starter during the pandemic, like everyone else on the planet, right? But I completely forgot to feed it, and it turned this horrible gray color and smelled like old gym socks. 

Anyway... wait, what were we just talking about? Did you ask about my stakeouts?
Did you have trouble with sitting still and focusing when you were in high school?

High school? Oh, yeah, definitely. Even before that, actually. My grade-school report cards always said I was bright but couldn't stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother still jokes that I treated every classroom like a crime scene I had to pace through. She actually kept all those old report cards in this big plastic tub in her basement. 

Speaking of her basement, it flooded last spring during those massive rainstorms. It was a total disaster. We spent three days hauling out ruined cardboard boxes. You really shouldn't store things in cardboard if you live in a flood zone, you know? You have to use those heavy-duty plastic bins with the latching lids. I bought a bunch of them at the hardware store when I was helping her clean up. The hardware store near her house is one of those old-fashioned ones with the wooden floors that creak when you walk on them. I love that sound. It reminds me of this old Victorian house I investigated once for an insurance fraud case. The guy claimed his antique collection was stolen, but I found half of it hidden in his own attic. The attic had these beautiful stained glass windows, though. Real Tiffany glass, I think. Or maybe it was a reproduction. I'm not really an expert on antiques, honestly, I just know what looks nice. 

Anyway... wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my mom's house?
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?

Interrupt? Um, I guess I do, yeah. It happens a lot at work, actually. If I hear the junior detectives discussing a lead, or even just my neighbors talking in the hallway outside my apartment, I just kind of jump right in. I'll start throwing out questions or giving advice before anyone even asked me to. And then a few minutes later, I'll realize I completely barged into a conversation that had nothing to do with me. 

My neighbors were actually just talking about the garbage pickup schedule the other day, which is completely confusing now. They changed it so recycling is only every other Tuesday, but yard waste is on Thursdays? It makes no sense. I ended up putting my recycling bin out on the wrong day and getting a citation from the homeowner's association. The HOA president is this woman named Susan who measures the grass with a ruler. Literally, a ruler. She came over once to complain about my wind chimes being too loud. I bought them at this little craft fair downtown. The artisan who made them used recycled sea glass, and they're gorgeous. The blue ones look just like the ocean. I love the ocean, but I burn so easily. I have to wear SPF 100 if I'm even thinking about going to the beach. I bought this special reef-safe sunscreen last summer, but it leaves this horrible white film all over your skin. You look like a ghost. 

Anyway... wait, what was the question? Did you ask if I like the beach?
Do you think your main difficulty is paying attention or being overly active?

Honestly, I'm not really sure. I haven't really thought about which one is the main problem. I guess I'm just kind of... both? Or maybe neither? I don't know, it's hard to separate them out, you know? 

Like, when I'm trying to figure out a case, my brain is going a million miles an hour, which I guess is the active part. But then I'll be looking at a suspect's financial records—which are incredibly boring, by the way, just pages and pages of bank statements. I had this one case where the guy was embezzling from his own brother's car dealership. A dealership! Who even buys new cars right now with the interest rates being what they are? I've been driving the same sedan for eight years. It's got this weird rattle in the dashboard that my mechanic swears he can't hear, but I know it's there. It only happens when I go over 45 miles an hour. I think it might be a loose screw near the air vent. I tried to fix it myself with a screwdriver I got in one of those cheap little kits from the dollar store, but the handle snapped right off. You really get what you pay for with tools. My dad always said you should invest in a good set of socket wrenches. He kept his in this pristine red metal toolbox in the garage. He was so organized. I try to be organized, I really do, but my desk always ends up looking like a paper explosion. 

Wait, sorry... what were you asking me? Was it about my car?
Do you think your trouble with sitting still is more because you're bored or because you have excess energy?

Bored or excess energy? Um, I don't really know if it's one or the other. I've never really stopped to analyze why I can't sit still, to be honest. I just know that if I'm in a chair for too long, my legs start doing this bouncing thing, or I have to get up and pace. 

I do a lot of pacing when I'm on stakeouts. Well, not pacing, obviously, because you're in a car, but I'll be tapping the steering wheel or fiddling with the radio dial. Stakeouts are the worst part of being a PI. Everyone thinks it's like the movies where you're constantly in high-speed chases, but mostly it's just sitting in a hot car drinking lukewarm coffee and waiting for someone to leave their house. I usually get my coffee from this little drive-thru place near my apartment. They have these amazing blueberry muffins, but they always run out by 9 AM. You have to get there super early. I tried baking my own muffins once during lockdown. I bought all these fancy silicone baking cups because they're supposed to be non-stick, but the batter just stuck to them anyway. Plus, they're a nightmare to wash. You have to turn them completely inside out to get the crumbs out of the little ridges. I ended up just throwing them away and going back to the paper liners. The paper ones with the little metallic patterns on the outside are the best. I found some with tiny silver stars on them for a friend's birthday party last year. She turned 50 and had this huge blowout bash at a rented hall...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Was it about my job?
Did your trouble with sitting still and focusing start when you were a child or did it begin later in life?

Oh, definitely when I was a child. It's not a new thing at all. Like, my grade-school report cards always said the exact same thing—that I was bright but I just couldn't stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother still jokes about it, actually. She says I treated every single classroom like a crime scene that I had to pace through and inspect. 

Which is funny, because real crime scenes are way less exciting than people think. Mostly it's just yellow tape and standing around waiting for someone else to do their job. Speaking of yellow tape, they completely blocked off the sidewalk in front of my apartment building yesterday for some kind of water main repair. It's a total disaster. I had to walk three extra blocks just to get to the grocery store, and of course, it started pouring rain, and I didn't have my umbrella. I have this really great umbrella, too—it's one of those reverse-folding ones so the water doesn't drip all over your floorboards when you get in the car. I bought it off an infomercial at like two in the morning. I usually never buy things from TV, but I couldn't sleep, and the guy selling it was just so incredibly persuasive. He had this whole demonstration with a wind tunnel and everything. It came in a two-pack, so I gave the second one to my sister, but she lost hers on the subway... 

Wait, sorry, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Was it about my mom?
Do you think your trouble with sitting still is more because you have a lot of energy or because you get distracted easily?

Energy or distraction? Gosh, probably the energy. I just feel like I always have this motor running inside me. Like, even on days when I don't have any field work, I still move from unpacking boxes to reorganizing case files to running errands like I'm chasing a lead. I just have a really hard time being off duty, you know? 

Speaking of unpacking boxes, I just got this massive shipment of manila folders because my local office supply store went out of business and had a clearance sale. It's such a shame they closed, too. The owner, Mr. Henderson, was this sweet older guy who used to give my dog a little treat every time we walked by. I have a terrier mix, Buster. He’s got this wiry hair that gets absolutely everywhere. I actually had to buy a special vacuum cleaner just for the pet hair. It’s one of those robot ones that just bumps into the walls all day. I caught Buster barking at it yesterday while it was stuck under the sofa. It just kept spinning its little side brushes and beeping this sad little tune. I tried to pull it out, but it had snagged on a rogue sock. I don't even know where the sock came from, because I only buy black ankle socks and this one was neon green with little tacos on it. My nephew must have left it here when he visited for Thanksgiving. He's twelve now and going through this phase where he only eats food if it's shaped like a dinosaur...

Wait, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I totally lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Was it about my dog?
Do you think you have more trouble paying attention to details or controlling your physical activity?

Oh, definitely the physical activity. Like, when I'm stuck at my computer combing through records for a case, my foot is just constantly bouncing under the desk. I'll be clicking a pen non-stop, or shifting around in my chair so much that I actually lose my place in whatever I'm reading. It's really frustrating, especially with the pen clicking, because I actually broke my favorite pen doing that last week. 

It was one of those nice, heavy metal ones that I accidentally walked out of a diner with when I was interviewing a witness. The diner was this great little retro place over on 4th street that makes incredible cherry pie. Real cherries, you know, not that canned gelatin stuff. I tried making a cherry pie from scratch for the Fourth of July a couple of years ago, and getting the pits out is a total nightmare. I bought a special cherry pitter gadget online, but it just mangled the fruit and sprayed red juice all over my white kitchen cabinets. It looked like a horror movie in there. I had to use bleach spray to get the stains out of the grout, and the smell of bleach always reminds me of the community pool I used to go to when I was a kid. They had this huge high dive that I was absolutely terrified of, but my older brother dared me to jump off it, and he bribed me with a pack of vintage baseball cards. He was obsessed with collecting them, kept them in these pristine plastic binders... 

Wait, I'm sorry, I'm rambling again. What did you ask me? Was it about my computer?
Do you usually feel restless or have trouble sitting still when you're feeling stressed or upset?

Honestly, no, it's not really tied to my mood or being stressed out. I'm just always like this. Even when I'm completely relaxed, watching TV or whatever, I'm still fidgeting or getting up to pace around the living room. It's just a constant thing. 

Speaking of pacing around the living room, I finally got around to hanging up these framed maps I bought like three years ago. I found them at this huge flea market they hold out by the fairgrounds every summer. It's an amazing event, they have hundreds of vendors selling antiques and handmade stuff. I almost bought this incredible vintage typewriter there once, but it was missing a few keys. The guy selling it was wearing this massive cowboy hat, which was funny because it was like 95 degrees out with 100 percent humidity. You'd think he'd want a straw hat or something breathable, right? I actually got heat exhaustion that day and had to sit in the shade drinking this lukewarm lemonade for an hour. The lemonade stand was run by these teenagers who were clearly more interested in texting than squeezing lemons. Kids these days are just glued to their phones. My neighbor's daughter walked straight into a stop sign last week because she was looking down at a screen. She had this huge bruise on her forehead that looked exactly like a plum...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. What was the question? Was it about being stressed?
Have you ever been diagnosed with or considered having Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder?

No, I've never been diagnosed with anything like that, or even really thought about it until recently. I just always figured I was a high-energy person, you know? Like, I need a job where I'm moving around and doing different things. 

Speaking of moving around, I actually started taking this salsa dancing class on Tuesday nights to try and burn off some of that extra energy. It's so much fun, but the instructor is this incredibly intense guy from Argentina who takes the footwork way too seriously. He actually yelled at me last week because I was doing a cha-cha step instead of a basic salsa step. But honestly, the music is so loud in that studio, you can barely hear the beat anyway. They have these huge, blown-out speakers in the corners that vibrate the whole floor. The floor is this gorgeous old hardwood, though. It reminds me of the floors in this historic mansion I had to stake out for a case a few years back. We were trying to catch this guy who was faking a back injury for an insurance claim, and I had to sit in my car across the street for three days straight eating nothing but stale pretzels and drinking lukewarm coffee. I hate lukewarm coffee. I finally bought one of those insulated travel mugs that keeps it piping hot for hours, but I always forget to wash the lid, and then it gets this weird, funky smell that's impossible to get out...

Wait, sorry. I totally lost track again. What did you ask me? Was it about my job?
Do you think your main difficulty is with paying attention or with being overly active?

Oh, definitely the being overly active part. Like, even on days when I don't have field work and I'm supposed to be taking it easy, I still move from unpacking boxes to reorganizing my case files to running errands like I'm actively chasing a lead. I just have a really hard time being off duty. 

Speaking of being off duty, I tried to actually take a real vacation last month. I booked this little cabin up by the lake, thinking I'd just read and relax. But the cabin had this weird draft coming from the window, and before I knew it, I was at the local hardware store buying weather stripping and a caulking gun. The guy at the hardware store was so helpful, though. He had this amazing golden retriever that just hung out behind the counter. I love dogs, but I could never have one with my schedule. My sister has three dogs, and her house is absolute chaos. She just got a new puppy that chewed through her expensive rug. It was a Persian rug, hand-woven, beautiful colors—deep reds and blues. I always wanted a rug like that for my office, but I know I'd just end up rolling my chair over it and ruining the edges. My office chair is already falling apart, actually. The wheels squeak constantly, and I tried WD-40, but it just made my hands smell like chemicals for two days...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? What was the question? Was it about my days off?
Do you think your main difficulty is with staying still and controlling your movements or with paying attention and following instructions?

Yeah, it's definitely the staying still part. Even when I'm supposed to be sitting quietly, I'm not really still. Like when I'm stuck at the computer combing through records for a case, my foot is just constantly bouncing under the desk, or I'm clicking a pen, or I'm shifting around in my chair so much that I actually lose my place in whatever I'm reading. 

Speaking of reading, I tried to start this new mystery novel last week because my friend recommended it. She's in this book club that meets every Thursday at this little Italian restaurant downtown. They have the best garlic bread there, it's always perfectly crispy on the edges but soft in the middle. I tried to make garlic bread at home once, but I totally burned it because I got distracted trying to fix a leaky faucet in the bathroom. Plumbers are just so expensive, you know? I called one last month and he wanted like two hundred dollars just to come look at it. He drove this huge bright yellow van with a giant cartoon wrench painted on the side. It was so obnoxious. I don't know why companies do that, it's like they want to be an eyesore. Kind of like this neon sign they just put up at the diner across from my apartment. It flashes this bright pink light right into my bedroom window all night long. I had to buy these heavy blackout curtains, but they're so heavy that the curtain rod actually pulled out of the drywall. Now I have these two gaping holes in my wall that I need to patch...

Wait, sorry, I completely lost the thread. What did you ask me? Was it about sitting at the computer?
Do you think your difficulties are more related to problems with attention or to being overly active?

Well, like I said, it's really the being overly active part. I just can't seem to turn it off, you know? It's like my motor is always running, even when I'm just trying to relax. 

Speaking of relaxing, I actually tried to take up knitting a few years ago because I read somewhere that it's supposed to be really meditative. I bought all this beautiful, expensive yarn—this really soft merino wool in this deep emerald green. Green is my favorite color, it reminds me of the forest. I love hiking, but I haven't been in ages because my hiking boots got completely ruined on a case. I was tracking this guy who was supposed to be in a wheelchair, but he was actually out hiking the Appalachian Trail. Can you believe the nerve of some people? Anyway, I had to follow him through this really muddy section, and my boots just got caked in it. I tried to wash them in the sink, but the mud just clogged the drain. I had to use a whole bottle of Draino, and the smell was awful. It smelled like sulfur and bleach mixed together. It reminded me of this public pool I used to go to when I was a kid. The lifeguards there were always blowing those loud whistles...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. What did you ask me? Was it about my hiking boots?

doctor.question: Do you think your difficulties are more related to problems with attention or to being overly active?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking a general question about whether the difficulties are related to attention or hyperactivity. This was already answered previously with the 'Constant_Activity' symptom, and none of the remaining specific symptoms (Leaving Seat, Quiet Activity Difficulty, Excessive Talking, Interrupting) are directly targeted by this broad question.

patient.answer:
Well, like I said, it's really the being overly active part. I just can't seem to turn it off, you know? It's like my motor is always running, even when I'm just trying to relax. 

Speaking of relaxing, I actually tried to take up knitting a few years ago because I read somewhere that it's supposed to be really meditative. I bought all this beautiful, expensive yarn—this really soft merino wool in this deep emerald green. Green is my favorite color, it reminds me of the forest. I love hiking, but I haven't been in ages because my hiking boots got completely ruined on a case. I was tracking this guy who was supposed to be in a wheelchair, but he was actually out hiking the Appalachian Trail. Can you believe the nerve of some people? Anyway, I had to follow him through this really muddy section, and my boots just got caked in it. I tried to wash them in the sink, but the mud just clogged the drain. I had to use a whole bottle of Draino, and the smell was awful. It smelled like sulfur and bleach mixed together. It reminded me of this public pool I used to go to when I was a kid. The lifeguards there were always blowing those loud whistles...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. What did you ask me? Was it about my hiking boots?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of persistent restlessness, inability to stay still, and excessive fidgeting, along with a history of similar behavior dating back to childhood, align most closely with the diagnostic criteria for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Hyperactive-Impulsive Type.
